notes: Taken from the Board of Elections' 46-day election notice, which lists every contest and issue with the precincts that vote on it. Issue wording is the Board's summary; the full wording is on the sample ballot.

Candidates are listed alphabetically by last name, not in ballot order: Ohio rotates the order of names from precinct to precinct. Certified write-in candidates are not printed on the ballot and are not listed.

"Where you live" uses the state voter file: a district or school levy is shown for a city, village or township when any of its voters live in that district. Your exact ballot depends on your precinct.
The Board's notice does not give local issue numbers; see your sample ballot for them.

Piqua also holds a city special election on November 3, 2026 (three recall questions and a charter amendment), on its own ballot. The Board's special-election notice says the ward candidates' names would be published after October 16; they are not listed here.

issues.title: Charter amendment: prohibit construction of a data center
issues.text: Add Section 138 to the Piqua City Charter prohibiting construction of a data center: one or more buildings or facilities on a single or aggregated parcel used primarily for digital information services, with an aggregate monthly demand or peak load over 25 megawatts. The section is self-executing.
